record.title: NYU Shanghai report preserves a Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 RL dashboard snapshot
record.summary: A September 17 NYU Shanghai RITS report preserves a contemporaneous view of Xiaomi's public MiMo-V2.6 reinforcement-learning dashboard. It describes two runs, `mimo-v2.6-pro` and `mimo-v2.6-flash`, and reports that the dashboard showed about US$1.23 million cumulative spend, 27.6B and 35.2B processed tokens, long rollout contexts and intermediate DeepSWE scores. The page also showed run restarts associated with a VRAM issue and a dataset infrastructure error. These are dashboard values relayed by RITS, not independently audited telemetry. Xiaomi's dashboard currently renders only navigation labels, so current status and live values could not be checked.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NYU Shanghai RITS published a dated report describing a public MiMo-V2.6 RL dashboard snapshot from 17 September 2026 and attributed the dashboard image and values to Xiaomi MiMo.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: RITS reports that the dashboard showed two runs, `mimo-v2.6-pro` and `mimo-v2.6-flash`, and a cumulative cost counter of about US$1.23 million at its 17 September snapshot.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: RITS reports intermediate DeepSWE v1.1 avg@3 scores of 63.72 for the Pro run at step 10 and 60.77 for Flash at step 12, using Xiaomi's evaluation setup and mini-swe-agent harness; these were not independent leaderboard results.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: RITS states that the metrics were unaudited Xiaomi-reported values, that the model sizes and architectures were undisclosed, and that the current dashboard was not a final release or capability evaluation.

evidence_gaps.description: The dated metrics are preserved by a university report, while the live Xiaomi page currently exposes no telemetry; no company export or archived dashboard data was found in this review.
No independently run evaluation or audit of run counters, costs or checkpoint scores is available.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported telemetry is accurate, it gives researchers useful evidence about the costs, scale and operational failure modes of very large agentic RL runs, a consequential but narrow improvement in training-economics transparency. It does not establish performance or frontier capability, and the snapshot is secondhand and unaudited.
limitations: Numeric values are Xiaomi telemetry as reported by NYU Shanghai RITS from one dated snapshot; the underlying first-party dashboard no longer exposes them and no independent audit was found.
Intermediate DeepSWE scores used Xiaomi's setup and mini-swe-agent harness; they are not independent leaderboard entries and cannot be compared across different harness or attempt counts.
The report does not identify MiMo-V2.6 model sizes or architectures and does not establish final model performance, release details or comparative training efficiency.
The reported dashboard included run interruptions; the final status and eventual outcomes of the runs were not verified.

It describes two runs, `mimo-v2.6-pro` and `mimo-v2.6-flash`, and reports that the dashboard showed about US$1.23 million cumulative spend, 27.6B and 35.2B processed tokens, long rollout contexts and intermediate DeepSWE scores. The page also showed run restarts associated with a VRAM issue and a dataset infrastructure error. These are dashboard values relayed by RITS, not independently audited telemetry. Xiaomi's dashboard currently renders only navigation labels, so current status and live values could not be checked.

technical.claimed_result: RITS reports approximately US$1.23m combined run costs and specific token, rollout and intermediate DeepSWE figures from the 17 September dashboard snapshot; no independent audit was performed.
technical.compute_or_cost: RITS reports a dashboard counter of approximately US$1.23m across both runs at the snapshot, with about US$853k for Pro and US$378k for Flash; this is not an independently audited accounting.
technical.demonstrated_result: A university research institute published a contemporaneous account of the public dashboard and its Xiaomi-attributed screenshot; live values are no longer visible through the checked company page.
technical.implementation_status: Training runs were reported ongoing at snapshot time; their final outcomes and current status are unknown.
technical.mechanism: The company dashboard reportedly streamed reinforcement-learning run progress, rollout counts, step timings, costs, benchmark checkpoint scores, training metrics and infrastructure errors during two long-running agentic training jobs.
technical.regime: Two named MiMo-V2.6 RL runs (`pro` and `flash`) as displayed around 12:02 Beijing time on 17 September 2026. The model architecture and parameter sizes were not disclosed in the report.
technical.reproducibility: The report preserves a dated description and Xiaomi-attributed screenshot, but no raw telemetry export or run artifacts were available for reproduction.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline or independent model comparison. RITS cautions that its interim DeepSWE metrics used Xiaomi's evaluation setup and should not be compared across harnesses or attempt counts.

brief.title: NYU Shanghai report preserves a Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 RL dashboard snapshot
brief.why_it_matters: The dated snapshot offers a rare view into the scale, cost and infrastructure details of frontier-scale agentic RL training. If the counters are accurate, they help researchers reason about rollout-heavy training economics and operational failure modes. The snapshot does not establish final model capability, comparative efficiency or current training status.
